_readme: Reference conformer counts for the de-duplication benchmark.
TWO KINDS OF KNOWLEDGE LIVE HERE AND THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE.
'textbook' is a count somebody established independently of this code.
'computational_lower_bound' means: at least this many distinct minima
were FOUND under the sampling protocol below. It is NOT the number of
conformers the molecule has, and scoring must never treat it as an
exact target. Ethylmorphine's 12 means '>=12 found', not '12 exist'.
ENANTIOMER POLICY. rdMolAlign.GetBestRMS does not reflect, so
mirror-image conformers of an achiral molecule are counted
SEPARATELY by this pipeline. Pentane's textbook 4 unique conformers
(TT, TG, G+G+, G+G-) therefore reads as 5-6 here, because G+G+ and
G-G- are enantiomeric and cannot be superimposed by a proper
rotation. This is understood behaviour, not noise -- see the
Every SMILES is stereochemically defined. Racemic input embeds BOTH
enantiomers, which inflates the RMSD count and deflates the
energy-derived bound at the same time: measured on racemic ibuprofen,
19 'distinct' shapes against 5 distinct energies, neither meaningful.

sampling_protocol.convergence: rc == 0 required; non-converged embeddings are discarded
sampling_protocol.note: The lower bounds below were derived from distinct converged energies (0.05 kcal/mol apart) over runs of this protocol, which is independent of the RMSD comparison being benchmarked. use_small_ring_torsions shipped 2026-08-13 after an isolated OFF/ON gate (see README): it moved no reference here -- the bounds predate it and remain valid as lower bounds, since the flag only ever ADDS sampled shapes.

molecules.name: aziridine
molecules.convention: a three-membered ring has one shape
molecules.notes: The original bug: ten embeddings returned ten copies and the viewer reported 'Conformer 1/10' for every one.

molecules.name: 2H-azirine
molecules.convention: a three-membered ring has one shape
molecules.notes: THE OVER-COUNT CASE. About 2% of embeddings converge to a distorted minimum 10.7 kcal/mol up -- same connectivity and torsions, C=N stretched to 1.339 A from 1.246. The energy veto promoted that force-field artefact to a second conformer until _IDENTICAL_SHAPE_RMSD was added. Present so the corpus covers over-counting as well as under-counting.

molecules.name: benzene
molecules.notes: A rigid case with no ring strain, so an over-count here would mean something different from azirine's.

molecules.name: ethanol
molecules.convention: anti and gauche; the two gauche forms are mirror images
molecules.notes: One of the two molecules the shipped 0.5 A threshold was calibrated on, and one it gets right. Present to catch a regression, not to prove anything new.

molecules.name: butane
molecules.convention: anti and gauche; the two gauche forms are mirror images
molecules.notes: The calibration molecule. Its pairwise RMSDs are BIMODAL -- below 0.5 A or at 0.66 A, nothing between -- which is a property of butane and is why a threshold fitted here generalised badly.

molecules.name: 1,2-dichloroethane
molecules.notes: A second small anti/gauche case with heavier substituents, so the check does not rest on hydrogen positions alone.

molecules.name: cyclohexane
molecules.notes: THE MOTIVATING FAILURE. The 0.5 A RMSD criterion alone reports 1 -- it merges the twist-boat into the chair, calling a textbook two-conformer molecule rigid. This is the row the energy veto has to earn. Still true with use_small_ring_torsions: the flag lifts pre-optimisation diversity from 1 shape to 3, but chair and twist-boat still merge geometrically (RMSD 0.3747 < 0.5), so the count stays 2 and the veto stays load-bearing.

molecules.name: pentane
molecules.convention: TT, TG, G+G+, G+G- as UNIQUE conformers; this pipeline separates enantiomeric pairs and so reports more
molecules.notes: Deliberately kept despite the convention mismatch: it is the clearest case of the enantiomer policy above, and a run that suddenly reports 4 would mean GetBestRMS had started reflecting.

molecules.name: ethylene glycol
molecules.notes: Two rotatable O-H plus the C-C torsion. The classic case for keeping polar hydrogens in the comparison: heavy-atom-only RMSD collapses it to 2.

molecules.name: (S)-ibuprofen
molecules.notes: Stereochemically defined on purpose. The racemic SMILES embeds both enantiomers and makes both metrics meaningless -- see the readme.

molecules.name: ethylmorphine
molecules.notes: The C19H23NO3 morphine derivative from the bug report, which generated 'Kept 2 distinct conformer(s) of 10 embedded'. BOTH geometric measures are blind here: for the extreme pair (dE 17.87 kcal/mol) the ten largest displacements are all hydrogens, TFD reads 0.038 against a literature cut of 0.2, and the heavy atoms barely move.
molecules.tighter_bound_note: 12 is what a SINGLE run of the protocol finds without small-ring torsions; with them (shipped 2026-08-13) a single run averages 15 [10-18]. Pooling five seeds found 17 before the flag and 25 with it -- so the true count is at least 25. The reference is deliberately left at the pre-flag single-run figure: it is a lower bound, exceeding it is not a failure, and moving it with every sampling improvement would make the benchmark grade itself. This is also the molecule with the weakest seed-to-seed agreement (coverage 0.60 under the flag: the discoverable space grew faster than per-run yield), so its union grows fastest with sampling budget.
